sites.rationale: HTR6 is a 7-TM GPCR with no signal peptide; the topology landmarks place residues 1–28 extracellular and TM1 beginning at residue 29, leaving 28 residues of clearance from the prepend junction to the first TM helix. An N-terminal tag on a GPCR with no signal peptide can only sit at the single extracellular N-terminus (insert_after_residue = 0, residue_after = M), so the position is topology-derived rather than residue-validated. Python confirmed residue 1 = M and residue 29 = V (TM1 start), satisfying the ≥3-residue TM-clearance rule by a wide margin. L2 (same paper, same construct) is concordant and reinforces confidence. Full-length 5-HT6R bearing an N-terminal HiBiT tag expressed in HEK293T cells; surface accessibility confirmed with the Nano-Glo HiBiT Extracellular Detection System (PMC10083584). No specific residue number is named; 'N-terminal' on a GPCR lacking a signal peptide resolves to exactly one extracellular terminus (before residue 1).

literature_notes: The ledger contains two clips (L1, L2) from the same paper (PMC10083584) describing the identical construct: full-length 5-HT6R with an N-terminal HiBiT tag, surface-detected in HEK293T cells. Both clips ground the same single site; L1 is used as the primary supporting clip because it explicitly names the full-length construct and the extracellular detection system. No residue number is stated in either clip, but for a GPCR with no signal peptide the N-terminal prepend is the only possible extracellular N-terminal position, making the junction topology-derived. Three other extracellular loops exist (ECL1: 86–99, ECL2: 167–187, ECL3: 291–302) but no ledger line reports any insertion in them for HTR6 or a close ortholog, so no sites are proposed there. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are mentioned in the ledger.
